title: Configurable autonomy age gates report hard-coded default ages
observed_behavior: The pending-publish category compares row ages with configurable pending_block_seconds and pending_review_seconds but always says the item has been parked for 72 or 24 hours. The failures category likewise compares against configurable failure_operator_required_block_seconds but always says the failure is older than 72 hours. A current-hash probe configured both block thresholds to 60 seconds, triggered them at 60 seconds, and received two separate 72-hour messages.
expected_invariant: Operator-facing health evidence must state the effective configured threshold that actually triggered a review or block, especially when the policy accepts values from 60 seconds through 30 days.
root_cause: The branch conditions use AutonomyPolicy values while their message strings embed the three default durations as literals instead of formatting the effective policy values.
failure_scenario: An operator configures a shorter or longer unattended-work threshold. Autonomy health blocks or warns at the configured time but reports a different default age, causing the operator to misjudge backlog duration, question the evidence, or take recovery action based on an age that was never observed.
evidence: autonomy_health_publish.py lines 155-180 compare policy.pending_block_seconds and policy.pending_review_seconds while emitting literal 72-hour and 24-hour text.
Lines 271-284 compare policy.failure_operator_required_block_seconds while emitting literal 72-hour text.
autonomy_policy.py permits each age setting between 60 seconds and 30 days and CONFIG_KEY_GLOSSARY.md describes them as configurable thresholds.
Bundled-Python current-hash probe used 60-second pending and failure block thresholds; both resulting blocker messages still claimed 72 hours.
The 100-test focused diagnostics/queue/path rerun passed but no current test varies these configured ages and asserts the resulting message text.
existing_safeguards: The underlying comparisons use the configured values, so the block/review timing itself is enforced correctly.
Issue payloads carry age_seconds separately, allowing a technically skilled consumer to recover the observed row age.
safeguard_gap: The primary message contradicts the policy that triggered it, and neither the message nor its issue fields expose the effective configured threshold.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_autonomy_health.py covers clean, blocked, pending-publish, and old operator-required states under default policy values.
tests_missing: Non-default pending review and block thresholds render their effective durations.
Non-default operator-required age threshold renders its effective duration.
Boundary tests assert both age_seconds and human-readable threshold evidence.
recommended_remediation: Format messages from the effective policy values using a shared duration renderer and include a machine-readable threshold_seconds field in each issue. Add non-default minimum, ordinary, and maximum configuration cases.
remediation_risk: low: diagnostic text and additive evidence fields change; launch-gate comparison semantics need not change
validation_rung: Focused autonomy-health policy/message boundary tests plus the diagnostics suite; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from AUDIT-FIND-COORD-DIAG-007, which concerns the inclusive count comparison; this finding concerns truthful rendering of three configurable age thresholds and was not present in current finding fragments.
